1.reason: Least inertia = least mass; a cup of tea is the smallest mass.

3.reason: Net zero unbalanced force -> no acceleration -> constant velocity (rest is a special case).

4.reason: He throws something and recoils to shore; this is Newton's third law of motion.

5.reason: Pulling hands back increases contact time, decreasing the rate of change of momentum (and thus the force).

6.reason: An accelerated body's velocity and speed change with a force acting; 'always goes away from the earth' is the incorrect statement.

7.reason: Zero external force -> momentum is conserved (law of conservation of momentum).

8.reason: Escaping air pushes back, balloon pushes forward; action-reaction = Newton's third law.

9.reason: On braking, water continues forward by inertia of motion -> moves forwards.

10.reason: Ejected water exerts a recoil; the fireman must exert a force to hold the hose.

11.reason: Steady (constant) speed -> no acceleration -> forces on the ball are balanced.

12.reason: Conservation of momentum: lighter mass M/4, heavier 3M/4; (3M/4)v = (M/4)v_light -> v_light = 3v.

13.reason: FIXED (was B): coin falls behind => train accelerated, not uniform

15.reason: Action and reaction act on different (two distinct) bodies. (Options B and D are identical 'different bodies'; B chosen.)

16.reason: F = ma; doubling a doubles F -> factor of two.

17.reason: Cup and ball both in free fall -> apparent weightlessness -> reaction between ball and base is zero.

18.reason: Newton's second law: a force produces acceleration.

19.reason: a = F/m; to double a with F fixed, halve the mass.

22.reason: Force of gravity = true weight (i true); descending elevator with downward acceleration gives reduced apparent weight (ii true). Both correct.

23.reason: Newton's first law treats rest (A) and uniform motion (B) alike. -> A, B.

24.reason: Total mass = 3m pushed by F, so common acceleration a = F/3m. (a) Net force on X = ma = F/3, NOT F -> wrong. (b) Net force on Y = ma = F/3, NOT zero -> wrong. (c) Net force on X = F/3; block Z (rightmost) needs ma = F/3 to accelerate, which Y supplies to Z, so force by Y on Z = F/3 = net force on X -> CORRECT. (d) Force by X on Y must accelerate Y+Z (2m): 2m*a = 2F/3, NOT F/3 -> wrong. Answer C.

26.reason: Inertia is the tendency to resist any change in the state of motion.

28.reason: Statement 1 is true (single push < limiting friction, truck does not move); Statement 2 is false (forces on different bodies do not cancel). So 1 true, 2 false.

29.reason: Drops fly off tangentially due to inertia of motion.

31.reason: Largest inertia = largest mass; the school bag is the most massive.

32.reason: Two unequal forces cannot give zero; the minimum number of unequal forces with zero resultant is three.

34.reason: Bullet momentum/sec = 0.02*400 = 8 kg m/s -> recoil force = 8 N per second.

35.reason: Inertia depends only on mass; equal masses -> all have equal inertia.

37.reason: Two spring balances hooked in series and pulled by equal and opposite forces experience the SAME tension throughout the connected system (a spring balance reads the tension/force passing through it). Newton's third law / equilibrium of the connecting link makes both read the same value. So if A reads 1.5 N, B also reads 1.5 N. Answer D.

38.reason: Action and reaction act on different bodies, equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

40.reason: A jet engine works on Newton's third law (exhaust pushed back, jet pushed forward).

42.reason: Force is a vector -> needs both magnitude and direction.

43.reason: Frictionless surface + constant velocity -> zero net force needed = 0 N.

44.reason: Net force zero => acceleration zero (Newton's second law, F = ma) => velocity is constant. On a velocity-time graph constant velocity is a horizontal straight line = option D. (B is uniform acceleration, C is uniform deceleration, A is an irregular spike — all imply non-zero net force.)

46.reason: a = F/m = 12/3 = 4 m/s^2; change in velocity = a*t = 4*1 = 4 m/s.

47.reason: v^2 = 2as; same v and same retardation a -> same stopping distance for both.

48.reason: Tying bags counters the effect of inertia (they would otherwise lurch on braking/turning).

49.reason: Pulling hands back increases the time to slow the stone, reducing the force on the hands.
